title: Tarps Over The Market Aisle
description:
## Task

An outdoor market aisle runs from position 0 to position `length`. Each available tarp is a closed segment `[left, right]` that shelters every point between its ends; tarps may be hung over each other, and two tarps that merely touch at a point leave no gap. Return the fewest tarps that together shelter every point of the aisle, or -1 if some point cannot be covered. Inputs can hold 10^5 tarps, so a pairwise or exhaustive search will not finish in time.

## Input

- `length` — the aisle length.
- `tarps` — a list of `[left, right]` pairs with `left < right`, in any order. They may reach outside the aisle.

## Output

The fewest tarps (an integer); 0 if `length` is 0; -1 if the aisle cannot be fully covered.

## Example

```python
fewest_tarps(10, [[0, 4], [3, 7], [6, 10], [2, 5]])  # returns 3
fewest_tarps(10, [[0, 4], [5, 10]])  # returns -1
fewest_tarps(0, [])  # returns 0
```

## Constraints

- 0 ≤ `length` ≤ 10^9
- 0 ≤ number of tarps ≤ 10^5
- -10^9 ≤ `left` < `right` ≤ 10^9
signature: def fewest_tarps(length: int, tarps: list[list[int]]) -> int
